blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

- MM3-H. Les exécutions passent par `HandlePool.prun`, une fonction d'exécution prouvée correcte (`prun_reach`). - H38 : non exprimable. Le cas porte sur l'analyse d'un programme à branchement (vivacité sensible au flot, spec 3) ; le noyau n'a ni branchement ni analyse statique, et une exécution en ligne droite d'une branche n'est pas le cas.

## (d) Statut des théorèmes de `HandlePool`

| `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` | prouvé sur tout état de `PReach`, qui contient **toutes** les étapes du noyau, sous `DDSound` : une compagne `Modify` active d'un pool est la seule compagne active de ce pool |
| `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct` | prouvés |
| `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` | prouvé : l'état du noyau est le résultat d'un `endUse` accepté de l'entrée ; feuilles `Uninit` ; entrée libre, génération incrémentée |

Détail pour `pool_inv_preserved` :
- **Contre-exemple** `pool_inv_not_preserved` : `derive` du noyau depuis la compagne vers une entrée libre. L'entrée n'est pas vivante (deuxième clause) et l'autorité n'est pas une autorité d'entrée (troisième clause).
- **Contre-exemple** `pool_inv_cex_entry` :
  - un `derive` depuis l'autorité d'entrée, son usage ordinaire, viole la troisième clause ;
  - le ré-ancrage de `exitFrame` rattache à la compagne une dérivée survivante, sans opération sur la compagne. L'entrée reste vivante à sa génération courante : la deuxième clause n'est violée que dans la lecture « lignée par une autorité d'entrée étiquetée » ((f) 12).

## (f) Décisions non dictées par le matériel

Pool :
1. L'entrée de pool vit à côté de `S3` (`PS`), comme l'entrée d'arène mais hors du noyau. Les résolutions sont un registre fantôme (`Res`) portant les étiquettes de génération.
2. Les entrées sont les enfants du stockage, dans l'ordre des indices. `newPool storage internal` ne reçoit pas de liste d'entrées.
3. `allocSlot` choisit la première entrée libre.
4. Le « droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` » de `resolve` est la précondition de `derive` de la compagne, mode effectif compris. C'est ce qui donne « quels que soient les handles » (H31a).
5. Un handle dont l'entrée n'existe pas : `fail`.
6. `freeSlot` échoue (`fail`) pour un handle périmé ou d'un autre pool seulement ; une entrée libre de même génération n'est pas un échec.
7. « Couvre l'entrée » (`freeSlot`) : couvre une feuille de l'entrée.
8. `allocSlot` reprend les conditions de destination d'`issue`. La taille d'un handle n'est pas représentée : MM-03 n'a pas de tailles.
9. `unresolve` reçoit la compagne. Il libère les autorités d'entrée dans l'ordre enregistré, puis la compagne, et rejette si une libération l'est (y compris celle d'une entrée déjà libérée).
10. `newPool` reprend `NewArenaPre` à la lettre ; sa clause 4 ne lit que les arènes.
11. `PReach` contient toutes les étapes du noyau, et pas seulement `release`, `store` et `transfer`.
12. Lecture de `PoolInv` :

    - deuxième clause : « porte la génération courante » se lit comme une lignée passant par une autorité d'entrée étiquetée de cette génération.
    Les contre-exemples de (d) valent pour les deux lectures de la deuxième clause, celle de l'entrée vivante comme celle de la génération.

13. « Périmé » est lu deux fois. `resolve` et `resolveMany` échouent aussi sur une entrée libre (`HandleOK`), conformément à `resolve` ; la liste d'échecs de `resolveMany` dans le matériel ne cite pas l'entrée libre. `freeSlot` ne lit que l'identité et la génération. Témoin : `pool_free_entry_handle`. `pool_no_stale_access` énonce génération courante **et** entrée vivante, plus que « aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ».

## (g) Questions pour arbitrage

1. **`PoolInv`** n'est pas un invariant de l'extension ((d)). Deux voies :
   - restreindre l'extension : la compagne n'est pas utilisable par les opérations du noyau. Cela ne suffit pas : le ré-ancrage de `exitFrame` et la dérivation depuis l'entrée violent encore les clauses 2 et 3 (`pool_inv_cex_entry`) ;
   - ou réénoncer les clauses 2 et 3, par exemple sur les seules autorités d'entrée, ce que prouve `pool_no_stale_access`.
2. **`resolveMany Observe`** n'est jamais accepté par la construction du matériel : le `split` de la compagne exige `Modify` (O2), donc rejet sur un lot valide (`resolveMany_observe_rejected`, un exemple), `fail` sur un lot invalide, la vérification du lot venant avant. Est-ce voulu ?
3. **Deux pools sur le même `internal`.** `newPool` ne l'interdit pas (clause 4 de `newArena` lue à la lettre ; `pool_two_on_one_internal`). Le handle d'un pool résout alors une entrée que l'autre a libérée et réallouée, et un `freeSlot` de l'un termine le contenu d'une entrée vivante de l'autre (`pool_two_freeSlot_cross`). Symétriquement, `newArena` accepte l'`internal` d'un pool vivant (`arena_on_pool_internal`).
4. **Passage par valeur vers l'appelé** ((b) 1). Le noyau ne permet pas à l'appelé de prendre une valeur de l'appelant. Le scénario H16 le suppose. Faut-il le relier aux conventions d'appel de la Spec 3 ?
5. **H01.** Un paramètre `Observe` dérivé du paramètre `Modify` sur le même local est accepté à l'entrée (`H01_reborrow`). G1 ne contraint que l'origine des paramètres `Modify`, et les deux autorités sont apparentées (I1). Le verdict attendu « reject » vaut-il aussi pour ce cas ?
6. **W2.** Le déplacement d'une ligne exige la libération de toutes les autorités qui couvrent ses champs, donc des deux autorités de colonne issues du `split` (O4.4, (b) 3). Le scénario attend un déplacement accepté après la libération d'une seule vue : faut-il lire « la vue » comme l'ensemble des autorités de colonne, ou le déplacement comme champ par champ, après la libération de la seule colonne concernée ?
7. **W3.** Les blocs sont-ils émis vers des locaux, auquel cas `reset` reste rejeté après `endUse` de la structure, ou dans la structure ?
8. **H51.** Le blocage va au-delà de l'écriture : `v` ne peut plus être terminé par `endUse`, seule la sortie du cadre le libère. L'option 2 ne le prévient pas : la vue n'est pas auto-bloquée, la configuration est un cycle de deux autorités (`H51_options`).
9. **H42.** Le développement en ligne droite est accepté par le noyau ; le traitement de `defer` relève de la Spec 3.
10. **Pool non vivant.** `allocSlot` et `freeSlot` n'exigent pas un pool vivant (`internal` actif), et le matériel est muet. `resolve` l'exige par le droit sur `internal`.
11. **Coût de l'option 3.** La tâche mesure la localité à l'opération ; le matériel demande si la vérification est « locale à une fonction ». Un cycle de `Blocks` peut-il traverser plusieurs cadres ? Aucun témoin n'est construit dans un sens ou dans l'autre.
12. **`freeSlot` selon `endUse`.** Le matériel dit « reject si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue », ce que le modèle applique en entier. Deux conséquences :
    - sur le pool de H44, dont `internal` est un bloc d'arène, donc dérivé, détenu par la valeur pool hors de l'entrée, `freeSlot` est rejeté : `internal` est une autorité dérivée active qui couvre l'entrée hors d'elle (`EndUseAccessOK`, A6 ; `pool_freeSlot_derived_internal`). Le même motif vaut pour tout pool vivant dont `internal` dérivé est détenu hors de l'entrée ; le témoin est ce seul pool ;
    - le droit par `writeShared` sur des métadonnées `SharedMutable`, admis pour `freeSlot`, ne suffit pas : `endUse` demande `Modify` sur l'entrée (A2 ; `pool_freeSlot_shared_right`).
    La parenthèse du matériel (« aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ») désigne-t-elle les seules préconditions retenues ?
13. **Contenu d'une entrée allouée.** « Son contenu reste `Uninit` » suppose une entrée `Uninit` ; une entrée jamais utilisée d'un stockage écrit avant `newPool` est `Init` (`pool_allocSlot_content_init`). Faut-il que `newPool` exige un stockage `Uninit`, ou que `allocSlot` le constate ?

## Revue adverse

Quatre revues indépendantes, en lecture seule, une par angle demandé ; chaque constat a été vérifié avant correction.

- **Exclusivité et fidélité du pool.** Aucun contournement de `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` trouvé. Constats : `freeSlot` inutilisable sur un `internal` dérivé ou avec le droit `writeShared` ; pools et arènes sur un même `internal` ; double lecture de « périmé » ; contenu `Init` d'une entrée allouée ; nuance sur les lectures de la deuxième clause de `PoolInv`. Traités par des témoins (section « Observations » de `MM03.Horrors`), (d), (f) 13–14, (g) 3, 12, 13, et la docstring de `allocSlotEff`.
- **Jumeaux MM3-H.** Chaque rejet a la cause nommée et chaque jumeau est accepté. Constats corrigés :
  - H51 : cause du rejet direct ;
  - H07 : le faux écart « construction adaptée » est retiré ;
  - variante W3 : rétablie avec les vues rangées ;
  - H17 : jumeau minimal ;
  - H01 reborrow : passé en (b) 2 ;
  - W2 : attendu et obtenu selon chaque lecture ;
  - H22 : atteinte du jumeau énoncée ;
  - compte des lignes ;
  - H03 : note sur F4.
- **Mesure `NoLock`.** Décisions confirmées. Constats corrigés :
  - témoin de non-localité remplacé par deux états où le noyau accepte le pas ;
  - lecture du coût signalée ((f) 23, (g) 11) ;
  - rang du pas de H49 dans la docstring ;
  - raison de H51 pour l'option 2.
- **MM23-H.** Chaîne d'exécution et `simulation` sans lacune. Constats corrigés :
  - H06 : le rejet tient désormais par `OwnedRoot`, la région déclarée désallouable ;
  - H04 : octets initialisés et séquence lecture, écriture ;
  - H07, H09 et H05 : `ok` au pas par `step_ok_of` ;

  - H02 : persistance (`reset_kills_blocks_after`) ;

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 1. Corpus MM3-H — discipline d'accès

| H49 | Même cycle fermé grâce à une autorité auxiliaire puis `release` de l'auxiliaire | à arbitrer (§5) | N3 | passe 7 (`f7a_cycle_by_release`) |

## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)
## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Graphe de scène | Pool de nœuds `{data, parent : handle, child : handle}` sur une allocation ; deux nœuds liés dans les deux sens par handles ; `resolve` `Modify` d'un nœud, écriture de `data`, `unresolve` ; `freeSlot` d'un nœud encore désigné par le handle de l'autre ; `resolve` de ce handle ; `freeSlot` pendant une résolution active | tout `ok` ; `resolve` du handle périmé : `fail` ; `freeSlot` pendant résolution : `reject` |
| W2 | ECS archetype + sparse set | Archetype à deux colonnes (SoA) sur une allocation ; `split` des colonnes ; système A écrit la colonne 1 pendant que le système B lit la colonne 2 ; `resolveMany` `Modify` de trois entités distinctes d'un pool d'entités ; déplacement d'une entité vers un autre archetype (transferts des champs de la ligne) pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération | lectures et écritures disjointes `ok` ; `resolveMany` `ok` ; déplacement pendant la vue : `reject` ; après : `ok` |
| W3 | Arène de frame | `alloc`, `newArena`, trois `issue`, trois vues rangées (`store`) dans une structure locale ; `reset` pendant que les vues vivent ; `endUse` de la structure ; `reset` ; réémission | `reset` pendant : `reject` ; après : `ok` ; réémission `ok` |

## 6. Registre des obligations inter-spécifications

| Obligation | Destination |
|---|---|
| `stat` (composante concurrente des obligations opaques) ; transférabilité, partageabilité ; H39, H41 | spec 2 |
| Protection forte des paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; H27b ; H38, H40, H42 ; `defer` | spec 3 |
| `dec` (validité de représentation) ; `SameSizeAlong` ; une référence se range dans un emplacement de type référence ; `kind` comme point d'accroche ; le type d'un pointeur porte la forme d'une région non contiguë (le pointeur n'en désigne que l'adresse la plus basse) | spec 4 |
| `dec` (alignement des accès) ; taille d'un pointeur et encodage `decode` ; largeur des adresses et épuisement de l'espace ; débordement des générations ; placement (`PlacementOK`), jetons (`TokCompat`) | spec 11 |
| Traduction bas niveau de `noalias` | spec 13 |
| Obligation de libération attachée à certains types ; H43 | spécification des ressources |
| `DeclaredDisjoint` (disjonction des feuilles déclarées) ; `FreeCompat` ; représentation des métadonnées d'arène et de pool | bibliothèque |

## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence

0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.
1. Écarts du brouillon MM-03 trouvés au jalon 2 (passe 1, (f) 1–6) : utilisabilité des feuilles lues et écrites ; empreintes faites de feuilles ; une racine par `alloc` ; marques de mort transitives ; `RootLive` ; bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. Locaux d'`enterFrame` possédés directement par le cadre (O6, à écrire dans la v0.3).
3. Décisions 1 à 4 du jalon 2 : disjonction déclarée par feuilles ; pointeur d'une région vide ; adresse la plus basse ; feuille de référence de la taille d'un pointeur.
4. Théorèmes à énoncer : induction « toute feuille `Init` atteinte a été déclarée ou écrite » ; correspondance `Step` ↔ `Reachable`.

import Ern.MM23
import Ern.MM03.Horrors

/-!
# MM23-H: adversarial corpus of the refinement (jalon 3, step 3)

The cases of the jalon-3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` v2), §3. Each case is an execution of
MM-03 from `S3.init statics` translated by `simulation` (`Ern.MM23`): an `SimRun` built step by step
by `srun`, which checks each labelled step (`Step3`) and its obligations (`Oblig`) by `decide`, with
parameters fixed once for the run. The layout is computed from the places of the run (`autoL`): the
`n`-th root place has the allocation `n` (MM-02 identities are created in that order, K2), its
leaves 8 bytes each in index order; the allocation of each root has 8 bytes per leaf, aligned on 8
(`autoG`); roots listed in `z` have size zero (K1 (d), D2). Tokens, placement, pointer encoding and
the obligations `dec` (accesses aligned on 4 bytes) are those of the pass-2 run `CaseSim`.

H15 and H16 rest on decisions 2 and 3 of jalon 2, not applied to the draft: they are encoded with
the verdict obtained and marked "écart connu" (material §0, rule 8). H14 and H17 are not encoded
(jalon-3 report, (a)).
-/

namespace Ern.MM23.Horrors

open Ern Ern.MM03 Ern.MM23

/-! ## Executable translated steps -/

section Exec
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- `ok` outcome of a labelled MM-03 step (`Step3`: L1 and L2 envelope included), `none`
otherwise. -/
def step3exec (s : S3) : Op3 → Option S3
  | .derive src q m => if DerivePre s src q m then some (deriveEff s src q m) else none
  | .split src rs => if SplitPre k s src rs then some (splitEff s src rs) else none
  | .release a => if ReleasePre s a then some (releaseEff s a) else none
  | .transfer src dst => if TransferPre k s src dst then some (transferEff s src dst) else none
  | .depend q x => if DependPre s q x then some (dependEff s q x) else none
  | .enter ps ls => if NoOwner ls ∧ EnterPre s ps ls then some (enterEff s ps ls) else none
/-! ## Run R1: owned storage, pin, transfer, leak, exit (H03, H04, H07, H08, H09) -/

/-- Contracts of R1: `ExternalDone` for the leaf 3. -/
abbrev K1 : K := KT [] [] [3] [] []

/-- R1: frame 1 with the allocator 0 and the leaves `v` (1) and `w` (2), written; the storage 3,
allocated for `v` and written; 3 pinned; `transfer v w`; 3 unpinned; `endUse w`; exit. -/
def r1 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0] w, .write 1 [1] w,
  .alloc 0 1 [lf], .write 3 [3] w, .pin 3, .transfer 1 2, .unpin 3, .endUse 2, .exit]
def P1 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K1 [] (r1.map toOp)).s.P
def π1 : Params := piOf P1 []
/-- R1 before the transfer, after it, before the exit, at the end. -/
def r1a : SSt := sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 6)
def r1b : S3 := (step3exec K1 r1a.1 (.transfer 1 2)).getD r1a.1
def r1e : SSt := sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 9)
def r1f : SSt := sst K1 [] π1 r1

theorem R1_sim : ∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
    exec MM02.State.empty os = r1f.2.2 ∧ Repr π1.tok π1.ptok r1f.2.1 π1.L r1f.1 r1f.2.2 :=
  (sim_of (P := P1) (z := []) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)).imp
    fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1, h.2.2.1⟩

theorem R1_prefix : ∃ os, SimRun K1 Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW [] π1 (r1.take 6).reverse r1a.1
    r1a.2.1 os r1a.2.2 :=
  simRun_of (P := P1) (z := []) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)

theorem R1_step6 : Step3 K1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1b :=
  step3exec_sound (Ern.HandlePool.some_getD (by decide))

/-- **MM23-H03** (passe 2, `pinned_address_stable`). Transfer of a value whose owned storage is
pinned: the leaf 3 of the storage has a live allocation before and after the step, at the same
address (L8), and the MM-02 sequence of the transfer touches no allocation of the storage. Expected:
no MM-02 step on the storage, address unchanged; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H03 : LiveAlloc r1a.2.2 (π1.L 3).alloc ∧
    LiveAlloc (exec r1a.2.2 (assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2)) (π1.L 3).alloc ∧
    leafAddr (exec r1a.2.2 (assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2)) π1.L 3 =
      leafAddr r1a.2.2 π1.L 3 ∧
    ∀ o ∈ assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2, opAlloc o ≠ some (π1.L 3).alloc := by
  obtain ⟨_, ht⟩ := R1_prefix
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, by decide⟩ <;>
  first
    | exact (simulation_pinned (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (fun _ _ => trivial) (fun _ _ _ => trivial)
        topPlacement_ok (piOf_geom _ _) (fun _ => rfl) ht R1_step6 (by decide) (l := 3)
        (by decide) (by decide) (.inl (by decide))).1
    | exact (simulation_pinned (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (fun _ _ => trivial) (fun _ _ _ => trivial)
        topPlacement_ok (piOf_geom _ _) (fun _ => rfl) ht R1_step6 (by decide) (l := 3)
        (by decide) (by decide) (.inl (by decide))).2.1
    | exact (simulation_pinned (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (fun _ _ => trivial) (fun _ _ _ => trivial)
        topPlacement_ok (piOf_geom _ _) (fun _ => rfl) ht R1_step6 (by decide) (l := 3)
        (by decide) (by decide) (.inl (by decide))).2.2

/-- **MM23-H04** (passe 2, `transfer_copies`). Transfer of a value in place (`v` into `w`): its
MM-02 sequence is a read then a write; the range of `w` receives the bytes of `v`, provenance
included, and the bytes of `v` stay as they were, every one initialised; in MM-03 the source is
`Moved` and unreadable (I4). Expected: the same; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H04 : (assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2).map opTag = [0, 1] ∧
    rangeBytes (exec r1a.2.2 (assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2)) π1.L 2 =
      rangeBytes r1a.2.2 π1.L 1 ∧
    rangeBytes (exec r1a.2.2 (assoc π1 (.transfer 1 2) r1a.1 r1a.2.2)) π1.L 1 =
      rangeBytes r1a.2.2 π1.L 1 ∧
    (rangeBytes r1a.2.2 π1.L 1).map (·.all initB) = some true ∧
    r1b.I 1 = .moved ∧ ∀ a, ¬ CanReadLeaf r1b a 1 := by
  obtain ⟨_, ht⟩ := R1_prefix
  have hs := simulation (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (fun _ _ => trivial) (fun _ _ _ => trivial)
    topPlacement_ok (piOf_geom _ _) (fun _ => rfl) ht
  have hwf := (reachable_invariants (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) hs.2.2.2.1).1
  have hc := transfer_copies hwf hs.2.2.1 R1_step6 (sameSize_of (by decide)) 1 2 (by decide)
  exact ⟨by decide, hc.1, hc.2, by decide, by decide, fun a h => by
    have h2 := h.2.1
    rw [show r1b.I 1 = .moved by decide] at h2; cases h2⟩

/-- **MM23-H07**, `ok` (passe 1). The `alloc` of R1 is one allocation of MM-02, of the size of the
geometry of the new root (8 bytes, one leaf), with the outcome `ok` (`step_ok_of`). -/
theorem H07_ok : (assoc π1 (.alloc 0 1 [lf]) (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 3)).1
      (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 3)).2.2).map opAllocSize = [some 8] ∧
    AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 3)).2.2
      (assoc π1 (.alloc 0 1 [lf]) (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 3)).1 (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 3)).2.2) :=
  ⟨by decide, step_ok_of (k := K1) (statics := []) (P := P1) (z := []) (ops := r1.take 3)
    (KT_dd [] [] [3] [] []) (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- **MM23-H08** (passe 1, `leaked`). `endUse` of `w`, whose owned storage 3 is not freed: no MM-02
step; the storage is logically dead and not freed, its allocation live (a leak). Expected: the
same; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H08 : assoc π1 (.endUse 2) (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 8)).1 (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 8)).2.2 = [] ∧
    r1e.1.dead 3 = true ∧ r1e.1.freed 3 = false ∧ LiveAlloc r1e.2.2 (π1.L 3).alloc :=
  ⟨rfl, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- **MM23-H09** (passe 1). The exit of frame 1: one deallocation per automatic allocation of the
frame (its locals 0, 1, 2, with the frame token 101), each `ok` (`step_ok_of`), none for the owned
storage 3, still live afterwards. Expected: the same; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H09 : (assoc π1 .exit r1e.1 r1e.2.2).map opDealloc =
      [some ((π1.L 0).alloc, 101), some ((π1.L 1).alloc, 101), some ((π1.L 2).alloc, 101)] ∧
    AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 9)).2.2
      (assoc π1 .exit (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 9)).1 (sst K1 [] π1 (r1.take 9)).2.2) ∧
    DeadAlloc r1f.2.2 (π1.L 0).alloc ∧ DeadAlloc r1f.2.2 (π1.L 1).alloc ∧
    DeadAlloc r1f.2.2 (π1.L 2).alloc ∧ LiveAlloc r1f.2.2 (π1.L 3).alloc :=
  ⟨by decide, step_ok_of (k := K1) (statics := []) (P := P1) (z := []) (ops := r1.take 9)
    (op := .exit) (KT_dd [] [] [3] [] [])
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ## Run R2: arena, block written, transferred, read, reset (H02, H06, H13) -/

/-- R2: frame 1 with the arena value 0, the allocator 1, the leaves `v` (2) and `q` (3); storage 4
with the leaves 5 and 6, owned by 0, `internal` 4; the block 5 on `[5]` issued to `v`; the leaf 5

/-! ## Run R2: arena, block written, transferred, read, reset (H02, H06, H13) -/

/-- R2: frame 1 with the arena value 0, the allocator 1, the leaves `v` (2) and `q` (3); storage 4
with the leaves 5 and 6, owned by 0, `internal` 4; the block 5 on `[5]` issued to `v`; the leaf 5
written through the block; `transfer v q`; `read q`; `endUse q`; `reset`. -/
def r2 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1] w,
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)], .write 0 [0] w, .newArena 4 4,
  .issue 0 0 [5] 2, .write 5 [5] w, .transfer 2 3, .read 3 [3], .endUse 3, .reset 0 0]
def P2 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K0 [] (r2.map toOp)).s.P
def π2 : Params := piOf P2 []
def r2i : SSt := sst K0 [] π2 (r2.take 7)
def r2r : SSt := sst K0 [] π2 (r2.take 8)
def r2f : SSt := sst K0 [] π2 r2

theorem R2_sim : ∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
    exec MM02.State.empty os = r2f.2.2 ∧ Repr π2.tok π2.ptok r2f.2.1 π2.L r2f.1 r2f.2.2 :=
  (sim_of (P := P2) (z := []) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)).imp
    fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1, h.2.2.1⟩

/-- After an accepted `reset`, no authority derived from `internal` is active (MM-03.3 §6, O19.2):
the old blocks cannot be used (R4 with `ResetPre`). -/
theorem reset_kills_blocks {k : K} {s s' : S3} {i via : Nat} (h : ResetAtStep k i via s (.ok s'))
    {ar : Arena} (har : s.arenas[i]? = some ar) :
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s'.A.length, ar.internal ∈ s'.ancs j → ¬ s'.Active j := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  simp only [ResetAtPre, har, OptP] at hpre
  simp only [resetAtEff, har, resetEff, arenaSet]
  exact hpre.2.2.1

/-- The old blocks stay inactive after the `reset`, whatever the later steps of `Reachable`
(MM-03.3 §3–6: no step reactivates an authority, `Steps.keeps`). -/
theorem reset_kills_blocks_after {k : K} {s s' s'' : S3} {i via : Nat}
    (h : ResetAtStep k i via s (.ok s')) {ar : Arena} (har : s.arenas[i]? = some ar)
    (hs : Ern.HandlePool.Steps k s' s'') :
    ∀ j < s'.A.length, ar.internal ∈ s'.ancs j → ¬ s''.Active j :=
  fun j hj ha hact => reset_kills_blocks h har j (List.mem_range.2 hj) ha
    ((Ern.HandlePool.Steps.keeps hs).active hj hact)

/-- **MM23-H02** (to state: R4 and `ResetPre`). After `reset`, the old block 5 is inactive and
stays so whatever the later steps (`reset_kills_blocks_after` for every old block), so no safe
program reads through it (the read through it is rejected), while MM-02 accepts a read of its range:
the allocation of the storage is live and the bytes written through the block are initialised. In
R2 the block was already released by `endUse q`, which `reset` requires (O19.2). Twin: the same read
through the block before its end is accepted. Expected: no safe program reaches it, MM-02 would
accept it; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H02 : ¬ r2f.1.Active 5 ∧ Read3Step 5 [5] r2f.1 .reject ∧ Read3Step 5 [5] r2i.1 (.ok r2i.1) ∧
    (∀ s', Ern.HandlePool.Steps K0 r2f.1 s' → ¬ s'.Active 5) ∧
    LiveAlloc r2f.2.2 (π2.L 5).alloc ∧
    ∃ v, MM02.ReadStep CaseSim.obR (leafAcc r2f.2.2 π2.L .read 5) r2f.2.2 (.ok v) :=
  ⟨by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide), fun _ hs ha =>
    absurd ((Ern.HandlePool.Steps.keeps hs).active (by decide) ha) (by decide), by decide,
    read_ok_of (by decide) ⟨by decide, by simp only [CaseSim.obR]; decide, trivial⟩⟩

/-- Contracts declaring deallocable, with the authority 7, both the storage 4 of R2 and the region
5 of its block. -/
abbrev K2f : K := KT [] [] [] [4, 5] [(4, 7), (5, 7)]

/-- R2 under `K2f` before the transfer, and after the end of the block value. -/
def r2k : SSt := sst K2f [] π2 (r2.take 7)
def r2kt : SSt := sst K2f [] π2 (r2.take 10)

/-- **MM23-H06** (passe 1). `free` of the block on `[5]` is rejected in MM-03 even when the contracts
declare it deallocable and compatible: the region is a part of the storage, not an owned root
(`OwnedRoot`, A6), and its leaf lies in the allocation of the storage. Expected: impossible, not an
allocation; obtained: the same. Every state is reached under `K2f`. Twin: in the same run, once the
block value has ended, the `free` of the allocated storage 4 is accepted. -/
theorem H06 : Reachable K2f [] r2k.1 ∧ K2f.Deallocable 5 ∧ K2f.FreeCompat 5 7 ∧
    ¬ OwnedRoot r2k.1 5 ∧ FreeStep K2f 5 7 r2k.1 .reject ∧ (π2.L 5).alloc = (π2.L 4).alloc ∧
    Reachable K2f [] r2kt.1 ∧ FreeStep K2f 4 7 r2kt.1 (.ok (freeEff r2kt.1 4)) := by
  obtain ⟨_, -, -, -, h₁⟩ := sim_of (k := K2f) (statics := []) (P := P2) (z := [])
    (ops := r2.take 7) (KT_dd [] [] [] [4, 5] [(4, 7), (5, 7)]) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide)
  obtain ⟨_, -, -, -, h₂⟩ := sim_of (k := K2f) (statics := []) (P := P2) (z := [])
    (ops := r2.take 10) (KT_dd [] [] [] [4, 5] [(4, 7), (5, 7)]) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide)
  exact ⟨h₁, by decide, by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide), by decide, h₂, .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- **MM23-H13** (passe 2). The block value `v` holds a pointer (L6: the address of the leaf 5,
the provenance of the storage); after `transfer v q`, the range of `q` holds the same bytes, every
byte with that provenance, and the read of `q` returns them. Expected: provenance kept; obtained:
the same. -/
theorem H13 : rangeBytes r2r.2.2 π2.L 3 = rangeBytes r2i.2.2 π2.L 2 ∧
    (rangeBytes r2r.2.2 π2.L 3).map (fun bs => bs.all fun b => b == .init 0 (some (π2.L 4).alloc) ||
      match b with | .init _ p => p == some (π2.L 4).alloc | .uninit => false) = some true ∧
    ∃ v, MM02.ReadStep CaseSim.obR (leafAcc r2r.2.2 π2.L .read 3) r2r.2.2 (.ok v) :=
  ⟨by decide, by decide,
    read_ok_of (by decide) ⟨by decide, by simp only [CaseSim.obR]; decide, trivial⟩⟩

/-! ## Run R3: statics, read, `writeShared`, free, exit (H05, H10, H11, H12) -/

/-- Contracts of R3: the leaf 3 `SharedMutable`; the storage 4 deallocable with the authority 7. -/
abbrev K3 : K := KT [3] [] [] [4] [(4, 7)]
/-- One static leaf, `Init`. -/
def stZ : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true)]

/-- R3: the base frame reads the static 0; frame 1 with the allocator 1, `x` (2), written, and the
`SharedMutable` leaf 3; 4, `Observe` on 3, writes it by `writeShared`; the storage 4 allocated for
`x` by the allocator 1, then freed with the authority 7; exit. -/
def r3 : List Op3 := [.read 0 [0], .enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1] w, .write 2 [2] w,
  .derive 3 3 .observe, .writeShared 4 [3] w, .alloc 1 2 [lf], .free 4 7, .exit]
def P3 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K3 stZ (r3.map toOp)).s.P
def π3 : Params := piOf P3 []
def r3f : SSt := sst K3 stZ π3 r3

theorem R3_sim : ∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
    exec MM02.State.empty os = r3f.2.2 ∧ Repr π3.tok π3.ptok r3f.2.1 π3.L r3f.1 r3f.2.2 :=
  (sim_of (P := P3) (z := []) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide)).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1, h.2.2.1⟩

/-- **MM23-H05** (passe 2, `freeSound_derived`). `free 4 7`: one `DeallocStep` of the allocation of
the root 4 with the authority 7, compatible with the token of its provider 1 (L4: `FreeCompat`
instantiated by `FreeCompatInst`), `ok` (`step_ok_of`); the allocation is dead afterwards.
Expected: the same; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H05 : (assoc π3 (.free 4 7) (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).1
      (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).2.2).map opDealloc = [some ((π3.L 4).alloc, 7)] ∧
    FreeCompatInst Ceq π3.ptok (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).2.1 4 7 ∧
    AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).2.2
      (assoc π3 (.free 4 7) (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).1 (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 7)).2.2) ∧
    DeadAlloc r3f.2.2 (π3.L 4).alloc ∧ (r3f.2.2.allocs (π3.L 4).alloc).map (·.freeAuth) = some (some 7) :=
  ⟨by decide, by decide, step_ok_of (k := K3) (statics := stZ) (P := P3) (z := []) (ops := r3.take 7)
    (op := .free 4 7) (KT_dd [3] [] [] [4] [(4, 7)]) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide⟩

/-- **MM23-H10** (passe 1). The allocation of the static 0 is live after every prefix of the run,
frame exit included. Expected: never deallocated; obtained: live at every step. -/
theorem H10 : ∀ n ∈ List.range (r3.length + 1),
    LiveAlloc (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take n)).2.2 (π3.L 0).alloc := by
  decide

/-- **MM23-H11** (passe 1, R1). The read of the `Init` static leaf by the base frame: one read of
MM-02, `ok`. Expected: `ReadStep` `ok`; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H11 : assoc π3 (.read 0 [0]) (sinit stZ π3).1 (sinit stZ π3).2.2 =
      [.read (leafAcc (sinit stZ π3).2.2 π3.L .read 0)] ∧
    ∃ v, MM02.ReadStep CaseSim.obR (leafAcc (sinit stZ π3).2.2 π3.L .read 0) (sinit stZ π3).2.2
      (.ok v) :=
  ⟨rfl, read_ok_of (by decide) ⟨by decide, by simp only [CaseSim.obR]; decide, trivial⟩⟩

/-- **MM23-H12** (passe 1, R2). The `writeShared` of the leaf 3: one ordinary write of MM-02, `ok`.
Expected: an ordinary `WriteStep`, sequential; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H12 : assoc π3 (.writeShared 4 [3] w) (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).1
      (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2 =
      [.write (leafAcc (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2 π3.L .write 3) (w 3)] ∧
    MM02.WriteStep CaseSim.obW (leafAcc (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2 π3.L .write 3) (w 3)
      (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2
      (.ok ((sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2.write
        (leafAcc (sst K3 stZ π3 (r3.take 5)).2.2 π3.L .write 3) (w 3))) :=
  ⟨rfl, .ok ⟨by decide, by simp only [CaseSim.obW]; decide, trivial⟩⟩

/-! ## Run R4: declared disjointness (H01) -/

/-- R4: frame 1 with the structure 0 of the parts 1 and 2. -/
def r4 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, (some 0, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0)]]
def P4 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K0 [] (r4.map toOp)).s.P
def π4 : Params := piOf P4 []

/-! ## Run R5: pointers to empty regions (H15, écart connu) -/

/-- R5: frame 1 with the arena value 0, the allocator 1, the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 with the
leaf 6, owned by 0, `internal` 5; `issue []` to 2; `split` of the root of 3 into `[[]]`, then
`store` of that empty authority 7 into 4. -/
def r5 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1] w,
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, (some 5, none, 0)], .write 0 [0] w, .newArena 5 5, .issue 0 0 [] 2,
  .split 3 [[]], .store 7 4]
def P5 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K0 [] (r5.map toOp)).s.P
def π5 : Params := piOf P5 []
def r5f : SSt := sst K0 [] π5 r5

/-- Base address of the allocation `i` in `s2`. -/
def baseOf (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((s2.allocs i).map (·.base)).getD 0

/-- Address decoded from the range of the leaf `l` (L6, the encoding of the run). -/
def decodedAt (s2 : MM02.State) (L : Layout) (l : Nat) : Nat := CaseSim.pe.decode (bytesOf s2 L l)

/-- **MM23-H15**, écart connu (material §0, rule 8; decision 2 of jalon 2 not applied). Expected: the
pointer to an empty region has as address the base of the allocation of its effective anchor and
as provenance that allocation. Obtained in a translated run: `issue []` writes the address 0, with
the provenance of the storage of the arena (the allocation of the anchor `internal` 5); the `store`
of an empty region split from the root of 3 writes the address 0 without provenance. The bases of
those allocations are not 0. Not presented as passed. -/
theorem H15 : (∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
      Repr π5.tok π5.ptok r5f.2.1 π5.L r5f.1 r5f.2.2) ∧
    decodedAt r5f.2.2 π5.L 2 = 0 ∧ (bytesOf r5f.2.2 π5.L 2 0).2 = some (π5.L 5).alloc ∧
    baseOf r5f.2.2 (π5.L 5).alloc ≠ 0 ∧
    decodedAt r5f.2.2 π5.L 4 = 0 ∧ (bytesOf r5f.2.2 π5.L 4 0).2 = none ∧
    baseOf r5f.2.2 (π5.L 3).alloc ≠ 0 :=
  ⟨(sim_of (P := P5) (z := []) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide)).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.2.1⟩, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ## Run R6: a region whose head has not the lowest offset (H16, écart connu) -/

/-- R6: frame 1 with the arena value 0, the allocator 1, the leaf 2; storage 3 with the leaves 4
(offset 0) and 5 (offset 8); `issue [5, 4]` to 2. -/
def r6 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1] w,
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)], .write 0 [0] w, .newArena 3 3,
  .issue 0 0 [5, 4] 2]
def P6 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K0 [] (r6.map toOp)).s.P
def π6 : Params := piOf P6 []
def r6f : SSt := sst K0 [] π6 r6

/-- **MM23-H16**, écart connu (material §0, rule 8; decision 3 of jalon 2 not applied). Expected: the
pointer to the region `[5, 4]` has the lowest address of its non-empty leaves, that of 4. Obtained
in a translated run: the address of the head 5, 8 bytes above. Not presented as passed. -/
theorem H16 : (∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
      Repr π6.tok π6.ptok r6f.2.1 π6.L r6f.1 r6f.2.2) ∧
    (π6.L 4).off = 0 ∧ (π6.L 5).off = 8 ∧
    decodedAt r6f.2.2 π6.L 2 = baseOf r6f.2.2 (π6.L 3).alloc + 8 ∧
    decodedAt r6f.2.2 π6.L 2 ≠ baseOf r6f.2.2 (π6.L 3).alloc :=
  ⟨(sim_of (P := P6) (z := []) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide)).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.2.1⟩, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ## Run R7 and `fail`: `alloc` of size zero and failed (H07) -/

/-- R7: frame 1 with the allocator 0 and `x` (1), written; the storage 2 allocated for `x`, laid out
with size zero (K1 (d), D2: a shape of one leaf). -/
def r7 : List Op3 := [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0] w, .write 1 [1] w, .alloc 0 1 [lf]]
def P7 : List Place := (Ern.MM03.Horrors.run K0 [] (r7.map toOp)).s.P
def π7 : Params := piOf P7 [2]
def r7a : SSt := sst K0 [] π7 (r7.take 3)

instance : ∀ r r', Decidable (KNS.DeclaredDisjoint r r') := fun _ _ => instDecidableFalse
instance : DecidablePred KNS.Pinned := fun l => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ ([] : List Nat)))
instance : DecidablePred KNS.ExternalDone := fun l =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ ([] : List Nat)))
instance : DecidablePred KNS.Deallocable := fun l =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ ([] : List Nat)))
instance : ∀ p a, Decidable (KNS.FreeCompat p a) := fun p a =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable ((p, a) ∈ ([] : List (Nat × Nat))))

/-- The prefix of R7 reached under the contracts `KNS`, where no allocation is satisfiable. -/
def r7n : Ern.HandlePool.PS := Ern.MM03.Horrors.run KNS [] ((r7.take 3).map toOp)

/-- **MM23-H07** (passe 1). `alloc` `ok`: one allocation of MM-02, `ok` (R1, `H07_ok`); of size zero:
one allocation of size 0, `ok` (`step_ok_of`) in a translated run; `fail` (`K.Satisfiable` false,
`KNS`, on a state reached under `KNS`): the state is unchanged, and there is no labelled step
(`Step3` asks the outcome `ok`), so the translation has no step and no MM-02 operation. Expected:
`AllocStep` / no step / `AllocStep` of size 0; obtained: the same. -/
theorem H07 : (∃ os, AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW MM02.State.empty os ∧
      exec MM02.State.empty os = (sst K0 [] π7 r7).2.2) ∧
    (assoc π7 (.alloc 0 1 [lf]) r7a.1 r7a.2.2).map opAllocSize = [some 0] ∧
    AllOk Ceq CaseSim.obR CaseSim.obW r7a.2.2 (assoc π7 (.alloc 0 1 [lf]) r7a.1 r7a.2.2) ∧
    Ern.HandlePool.PReach KNS [] r7n ∧ AllocStep KNS 0 1 [lf] r7n.s (.fail r7n.s) ∧
    ∀ s', ¬ Step3 KNS (.alloc 0 1 [lf]) r7n.s s' :=
  ⟨(sim_of (P := P7) (z := [2]) (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide)).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩, by decide,
    step_ok_of (k := K0) (statics := []) (P := P7) (z := [2]) (ops := r7.take 3)
      (op := .alloc 0 1 [lf]) (KT_dd [] [] [] [] [])
      (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    Ern.MM03.Horrors.run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .fail (by decide) (fun h => h),
    fun _ hs => nomatch alloc_det hs.2 (AllocStep.fail (by decide) (fun h => h))⟩

end Ern.MM23.Horrors

import Ern.MM02
import Ern.MM03

/-!
# Refinement MM-03.3 v0.3 → MM-02 v0.4 (milestone 2, passes 1 and 2)

Representation of the abstract states of MM-03.3 (module `Ern.MM03`) by the states of the abstract
machine of MM-02 (module `Ern.MM02`), refinement of every operation of MM-03 (R6), and simulation
of an execution. Both modules are imported unchanged; a lemma they lack is proved here.

The arbitrages of the task are cited as `K1`…`K5` (pass 1) and `L1`…`L8` (pass 2, which replace
the K arbitrages where they say so). The rules of the specifications are cited as `MM-02.x`
(MM-02 v0.4) and `MM-03.3 …` (MM-03.3 v0.3 révisée). Out of scope: concurrency, finite addresses,
representation of the metadata of arenas, low-level translation. The decisions not dictated by the
texts are listed in the reports `formal/reports/MM23_v0.1.md` (pass 1) and
`formal/reports/MM23_v0.1_p2.md` (pass 2), section (c); the gaps between the drafts and their
texts, section (f) of the pass-1 report.
-/

namespace Ern.MM23

open Ern.MM03

/-! ## Allocations of the MM-02 state -/

/-- The MM-02 allocation `i` is registered (MM-02.2) and satisfies `p`. -/
def AllocP (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) (p : MM02.Alloc → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s2.allocs i = some a ∧ p a

instance (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) (p : MM02.Alloc → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    Decidable (AllocP s2 i p) :=
  match h : s2.allocs i with
  | some a =>
    if ha : p a then isTrue ⟨a, h, ha⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact ha hb'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb

/-- The MM-02 allocation `i` is registered and live (MM-02.2). -/
abbrev LiveAlloc (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = true)

/-- W2: frame 1, allocator 0, owners 1 and 2 of two archetypes, entity pool value 3, handle leaves
4, 5, 6. Archetype 7 (columns 8 with 9, 10 and 11 with 12, 13) owned by 1; archetype 14 (columns
15 with 16, 17 and 18 with 19, 20) owned by 2; entity storage 21 (entries 22, 23, 24) owned by 3,
pool on it. `split` of the archetype into the columns (10 and 11), the second written, a read view
12 on it; system A writes the first column while system B reads through the view; `resolveMany
Modify` of three distinct entities. -/
def w2o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .write 2 [2], .write 3 [3],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, (some 7, none, 0), (some 8, none, 0), (some 8, none, 0), (some 7, none, 0),
    (some 11, none, 0), (some 11, none, 0)],
  .alloc 0 2 [lf, (some 14, none, 0), (some 15, none, 0), (some 15, none, 0), (some 14, none, 0),
    (some 18, none, 0), (some 18, none, 0)],
  .alloc 0 3 [lf, (some 21, none, 0), (some 21, none, 0), (some 21, none, 0)], .newPool 21 9,
  .allocSlot 0 0 4, .allocSlot 0 0 5, .allocSlot 0 0 6,
  .split 7 [[9, 10], [12, 13]], .write 11 [12, 13], .derive 11 11 .observe,
  .write 10 [9, 10], .read 12 [12, 13], .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 0⟩] .modify]
def w2 : PS := run K0 [] w2o
def w2a : PS := run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12])
/-- W2 after the release of the read view 12 and of the column authority 11. -/
def w2b : PS := run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11])

/-- **W2** (§5b, ECS archetype and sparse set; Lib). Expected: disjoint reads and writes `ok`;
`resolveMany` `ok`; the move of the row (transfers of its fields) while a column view is active:
reject; after its release: `ok`. Obtained: disjoint accesses, `resolveMany` and the rejection during
the view as expected. After the release of one view, the move is still rejected under either
reading of "the view of the column": after the read view 12 alone, by the column authority 11
(O4.4); after the read view and the column authority 11, the field 9 of the row is still covered
by the other column authority 10. The move is accepted after the release of both column authorities
given by `split` (report, (b)). -/
theorem W2 : PReach K0 [] w2 ∧ TransferStep K0 12 19 w2.s .reject ∧ PReach K0 [] w2a ∧
    TransferStep K0 12 19 w2a.s .reject ∧ ActiveDerivedOutside w2a.s 12 11 ∧
    PReach K0 [] w2b ∧ TransferStep K0 9 16 w2b.s .reject ∧ ActiveDerivedOutside w2b.s 9 10 ∧
    PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .release 10, .transfer 9 16,

    by decide, run_reach (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- Regions of the entries of a batch: the footprint of each designated entry. -/
def batchRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)

/-- State after the compound borrow of a batch (material §4): the companion `s.A.length`, then one
entry authority per handle by `split` of the companion (MM-03.3 §3, O2). -/
def resolveManyS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  splitEff (deriveEff s pl.internal pl.storage m) s.A.length (batchRegions s pl hs)

/-- Entry authorities of a batch with their slot and generation: the `i`-th split authority has the
identity `c + 1 + i` for the companion `c`. -/
def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs

/-- `resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4): `reject`
when the right fails; then `fail`, state unchanged and no authority created (atomicity), when the
batch is not valid; `ok` with the compound borrow when the `split` of the companion is accepted,
`reject` otherwise (`noSplit`). -/
inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (ps : PS) :
    POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
      SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.ok { ps with
        s := resolveManyS ps.s pl hs m
        res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
          batchEntries ps.s.A.length hs⟩] })
  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → ¬ BatchOK pl hs →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.fail ps)
  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
  | noSplit {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
      ¬ SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject

/-- K3, the decidable part of the relation of representation between an MM-03 state `s3` and an
MM-02 state `s2`, for the layout `L`, the frame tokens `tok`, the provider tokens `ptok` and the
ghost `provOf` (L4: a root allocated by `alloc` ↦ its provider):
- `lwf`: `LayoutWF` (K1);
- `inj`: two distinct root places are in distinct allocations (K2: a root corresponds to an
  allocation; a part to a sub-range of the allocation of its root, by `LayoutWF.sameAlloc`);
- `tokens`: the allocation of a root owned by the frame `f` has the token `tok f` (K2);
- `provTokens`: the allocation of a root allocated from the provider `pr` has the token `ptok pr`
  (L4);
- `live`: every usable root has its allocation live (K3);
- `init`: every `Init` leaf has all its bytes initialised (K3; L3: a `Moved` or `Uninit` leaf
  imposes nothing);
- `freed`: a root dead by `free` has its allocation dead (K3);
- `exited`: a root dead by the exit of its frame has its allocation dead (K3);
- `leaked`: a root owned by a place, not usable and not freed keeps its allocation live (K3 for a
  root dead by `endUse`; L5 for owned storage that dies with a freed root or with its frame).
It does not read the contracts `K` (L3). -/
structure ReprB (tok ptok : Nat → Nat) (provOf : Nat → Option Nat) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3)
    (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop where
  lwf : LayoutWF L s3 s2
  have := hR.provTokens p hp.1 hp
  rw [hpr] at this
  exact (this l hl).mono fun _ h => ⟨_, h, hc⟩

/-- R6 for `free` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O13; K4: `free` ↦ `DeallocStep` of the allocation of the root,
authority `auth`; L4: `FreeCompat` instantiated by `Compatible auth (ptok (provOf p))`; L5: one
`DeallocStep`, the storage owned by `p` keeps its allocation live): under `WF3`, the deallocation
has the outcome `ok` and the arrival states are in `Repr`. -/
theorem r6_free {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat} {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3}
    {s2 : MM02.State} {p auth : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2)
    (hfc : k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C ptok provOf p auth)
    (h : FreeStep k p auth s3 (.ok s3')) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 (deallocOps [rootAlloc L s3.P p] auth) ∧
      Repr tok ptok provOf L s3' (exec s2 (deallocOps [rootAlloc L s3.P p] auth)) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hdl, hfc', hu, hor, -⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h

## (a) Clause → déclaration

| Clause | Déclarations |
|---|---|
| K1, disposition paramétrique | `Layout` (feuille ↦ `MM02.Place` : allocation, décalage, taille) |
| K1 (a) feuilles d'une racine, une allocation | `LayoutWF.sameAlloc`, `rootAlloc`, `rootAlloc_eq` |
| K1 (b) plages disjointes | `LayoutWF.disjoint` (`MM02.RangeDisjoint`) |
| K1 (c) plage incluse dans son allocation | `LayoutWF.within` |
/-! ## Layout (K1) -/

/-- K1: layout of the leaves. The leaf `l` occupies the byte range `L l` of an MM-02 allocation:
its identity `alloc`, an offset `off` and a size `len` (an MM-02.4 place). The layout fixes no
ABI, no type alignment and no order of fields. It is a parameter of an execution, defined on
every index, present or future. -/
abbrev Layout := Nat → MM02.Place

/-- K1, obligations `LayoutWF` of a layout in an MM-03 state `s3` and an MM-02 state `s2`:
(a) the leaves of one root place are in one allocation; (b) two distinct leaves in one allocation
have disjoint ranges (`RangeDisjoint`, MM-02.2); (c) the range of every leaf lies within its
allocation, which is registered (MM-02.B, spatial containment). (d) No size is bounded below: a
range may be empty, so a shape of one leaf may have size zero. No other hypothesis. -/
structure LayoutWF (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop where
  sameAlloc : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
    ∀ l' ∈ footprint s3.P r, (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc
  disjoint : ∀ l < s3.P.length, ∀ l' < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' → l ≠ l' →

findings.location: formal/reports/J3_v0.1.md:139-142 ((b) 3), :253 ((g) 6), :297 (second-check summary); same claim in the W2 docstring, formal/Ern/MM03/Horrors.lean:840-848
findings.claim: The new claim that releasing one view is not enough "sous aucune lecture de « la vue de colonne »", and the (g) 6 premise that a move needs both split column authorities released, come from how this run was built, not from the scenario. The construction keeps system A's column authority 10 active through the move. If A's column is released after its write, leaving only one column view active as the material describes, the expected verdict holds under the column-authority reading.
findings.evidence: Material §5b W2: "déplacement ... pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération" (one view). Scratch file run with `lake env lean`, all decided with no error: `def w2c : PS := run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 10])`; `PReach K0 [] w2c ∧ TransferStep K0 12 19 w2c.s .reject` (the move is rejected while view 11/12 is active); `ActiveDerivedOutside w2c.s 12 11`; `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 10, .release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19]))` (the move is accepted once that view, 11 with its derived 12, is released). Sanity control in the same setup: `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.transfer 12 19]))` fails with "Tactic `decide` proved that the proposition ... is false". So the read-view reading fails, but the column-authority reading succeeds once A's column is gone. That contradicts "sous aucune lecture" and the "donc des deux autorités de colonne" in (g) 6.
findings.fix: Rewrite (b) 3, (g) 6 and the summary line. The result depends on the reading and on whether system A's column authority is still active at the move. Under the column-authority reading with A's column released first, the expected verdict is obtained (add that witness). Under the read-view reading, it is not. Ask the arbitration question on that basis.
